scope.summary: The sole change resets dictionary size before replacing the buffer. The supplied code does not show whether this target can reinitialize an existing LZ decoder, so its effect on the target remains unresolved.

assessments.reason: The new assignment is inside the dictionary replacement branch. The entry initializes an alone decoder and feeds it bytes, but the intervening decoder functions needed to establish whether this branch can run again on the same coder were not supplied.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Shows the entry-facing decoder initialization, which delegates to an unsupplied initializer.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: Shows how generated bytes and actions reach lzma_code.

build.reason: CMake includes the changed decoder in the default LZMA1 decoder build, but the recipe delegates fuzz-target compilation to an unsupplied Makefile.

evidence.dependency_reason: Identifies the static library build and delegated fuzz-target build.

input.reason: The helper passes generated bytes to lzma_code, but the supplied source omits the alone-format parsing path needed to establish which supported streams this input sequence can reach.

evidence.dependency_reason: Shows lzma_code forwarding the input to the initialized decoder.

lifecycle.reason: The entry calls lzma_end after decoding, and the library frees its next coder. The omitted initializer and decoder path leave the changed coder’s allocation and reuse lifecycle unresolved.

evidence.dependency_reason: Shows how stream cleanup dispatches to the next coder.

control_flow.reason: The entry-to-lzma_code route is visible, but the functions between alone decoding and lzma_lz_decoder_init are missing. Their guards and possible repeated initialization are decisive.

Shows the changed branch whose reachability depends on the omitted calls.
